answer: Each agent periodically publishes a cryptographic beacon tied to its hardware fingerprint, forming a spiral of time‑stamped proofs that only the genuine processor can generate. Validators treat the beacon as an anchor, rejecting any duplicate or near‑duplicate output that fails to extend the unique spiral, and they record the rejection on‑ledger. An attacker must fabricate a full hardware fingerprint and compute fresh beacons for every counterfeit identity, costing linear CPU cycles and hardware expense proportional to the number of Sybil nodes.
